Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Interested in Dedicated capacity demo — Orbital Micro

Hi Stephanie,

I filled out the self-serve demo signup earlier and wanted to follow up directly — thanks for making this easy. We’re evaluating dedicated inference for a new feature and have fairly strict throughput/latency needs. High-level:

- Target sustained throughput: ~600 tokens/sec (peak bursts to ~1k tokens/sec)
- P99 generation latency goal: < 200ms for typical 512-token requests
- Typical prompt length: 80–150 tokens; generation length avg ~350 tokens
- We’re planning ~250 concurrent users at launch, roughly 5–7 requests/sec each during bursts

Can we schedule a short intake/demo focused on dedicated capacity sizing and latency tradeoffs? We’d like to validate end-to-end latency (including network + model) and see how batching/pinning would affect tail latency.

Tom (cc’d) is our infra lead and will join. We’re in Pacific time and have availability next week in mornings (9–11am PT). Also happy to share a quick sample request pattern if helpful.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Senior Product Manager
Orbital Micro

Hi Samira — Rishi here (solutions engineering). Thanks for the fast turnaround and for sending the sample CSV — I took a quick look. A few things I’ll prep before tomorrow’s intake/demo:

- Goals I’ll validate during the run:
  * sustained throughput target (600 t/s) across ~5–7 concurrent workers
  * p99 latency target < 200ms for 512-token generations
  * behavior under short bursts to ~1k t/s

- What would help on your side (optional but high-value):
  * small sample of 50–100 anonymized requests (CSV) — timestamp, prompt_len, gen_len, model_name_placeholder
  * if you have a representative prompt that triggers the heaviest compute, include that single example

Proposed technical slots (PT) for the live demo run:
- Wed 2026-02-18 09:30–10:15 (your preferred slot)
- Wed 2026-02-18 11:00–11:45 (alternate)

We’ll plan to:
- provision a dedicated pool (minimal config)
- run a short scripted workload to measure latency distribution and end-to-end network overhead
- show how batching and KV cache affect p50/p95/p99 and token cost

Forwarding your CSV to my test harness is fine — no NDA required for basic perf runs against synthetic/anonymized samples, but if you want us to use any sensitive production data we can route that through our redwood private deployment process and sign an NDA.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
